title: Pruvz Public Evidence Packet — action record
description: One recorded business action as the Pruvz product API reports it (the action details view, GET /api/actions/{actionId}): the action's business identity, its two separate state machines (execution and verification), the embedded immutable decision-time Policy Snapshot, the frozen verification timing resolved at acceptance (format 1.1.0), and the three deliberately separated value groups a reviewer compares — the server-derived expected outcome, the agent's unverified claim, and what independent system-of-record read-back actually observed.

actionId.description: Server-generated identifier of the business action.

agentId.description: The agent that requested the action.

runId.description: The demo/agent run this action belongs to.

correlationId.description: The business correlation key, e.g. the payment the refund belongs to.

actionType.description: The kind of business action, e.g. "refund".

crmTicketId.description: The CRM ticket the decision context referenced; null when none was asserted.

claim.description: The agent's unverified claim about its own execution outcome; null until a claim is recorded. A claim never decides the verification result.

expectedOutcome.description: Derived by Pruvz server-side from the decision and the immutable Policy Snapshot — never accepted as an agent input. Null until derived.

observed.description: What independent system-of-record read-back actually observed: the latest INDEPENDENT_READBACK evidence, summarized. Null means no independent observation was recorded yet — reported honestly instead of echoing the claim or the expectation.

executionStatus.description: Agent execution progress — what the agent reports. Separate from verificationStatus by design.

verificationStatus.description: Independent verification state — what Pruvz proved. Terminal results (VERIFIED, OUTCOME_MISMATCH, VERIFICATION_FAILED) are assigned only after independent system-of-record read-back, never through any agent-facing contract.

finalOutcome.description: The proven business outcome, e.g. REFUND_SUCCEEDED. Present exactly when verificationStatus is VERIFIED; a mismatch or a technical failure never fabricates one.

verificationFailure.description: Why verification failed. Present exactly when verificationStatus is VERIFICATION_FAILED: a technical description of an unreadable source, never a business result.

reviewState.description: Whether the action needs, awaits, or received a human review decision. Only a terminal verification result determines it.

mismatch.description: The expected-versus-observed dimensions behind an OUTCOME_MISMATCH ruling. Present exactly when verificationStatus is OUTCOME_MISMATCH; a technical failure never carries one.

verificationTiming.description: The action's frozen verification timing (format 1.1.0): resolved exactly once when the action was accepted and never re-resolved, so later policy or configuration changes cannot affect an in-flight action. deadlineAtUtc null means no verification deadline was resolved — such an action can never produce a time-based mismatch and is reported as "verification deadline not configured". Null only on action records that predate the timing model.

verificationCompletedAtUtc.description: When the terminal verification result was assigned; null while verification has not concluded.

allOf.$comment: VERIFIED carries the proven outcome and nothing else: no failure block, no mismatch block, and review is not required.
OUTCOME_MISMATCH carries its mismatch dimensions and awaits or received a human ruling; nothing was proven, so no final outcome and no failure block.
VERIFICATION_FAILED is a technical outcome: it carries the failure block and never a business result or a mismatch story.
Before verification concludes nothing terminal may appear: no outcome, no failure, no mismatch, no completion time, and the need for review is honestly undetermined.

utcTimestamp.description: A UTC timestamp: RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 with the Z (Zulu) UTC designator, matching the *AtUtc field names. Local-offset forms such as +03:00 are not valid in this contract.

money.description: An amount of money in a single ISO 4217 currency.

subject.description: The business entity the action operates on.

decision.description: What the policy evaluation approved. Its amount is the decision amount, never a verified amount.

observed.description: The latest independent read-back observation, summarized. Field names match the evidence timeline items so this block can be correlated with its timeline entry.

verificationTiming.description: The frozen verification timing (format 1.1.0): the technical clock (when the first read-back is meaningful, how often absence is re-checked) and the business clock (the resolved verification deadline with its provenance). Spans are integer seconds so consumers never parse a duration format.

deadlineAtUtc.description: When the business window closes; null when no deadline was resolved — absence then never becomes a time-based mismatch.

deadlineSource.description: Where the deadline came from, in resolution precedence order: POLICY (the decision-time Policy Snapshot), TENANT_OVERRIDE (explicit tenant/action configuration), PRODUCT_SPEC (the product's per-action-type default — which may also be an explicit no-deadline decision), or NOT_CONFIGURED (no source resolved a deadline).

resolvedAtUtc.description: The acceptance moment the resolution was made and the deadline anchored to.

allOf.$comment: A POLICY or TENANT_OVERRIDE provenance always carries a concrete deadline.
NOT_CONFIGURED means no source resolved a deadline, so none may appear.

businessDiscrepancy.description: The monetary business discrepancy of one mismatch, or its explicit absence: when evaluable is false there is no amount at all — an unknown discrepancy is never rendered as a zero, because "no amount" and "zero amount" are different business statements.

mismatch.description: The review classification and expected-versus-observed dimensions behind one OUTCOME_MISMATCH ruling. The observed side is stated as recorded business facts (refund counts, ticket statuses), never as source payload contents.

mismatchReason.description: The temporal mismatch category (format 1.1.0): CONTRADICTORY_EVIDENCE means positive evidence contradicts the claim, assigned immediately with no deadline wait; EXPECTED_OUTCOME_ABSENT_AFTER_DEADLINE means the expected outcome never appeared and the resolved verification deadline passed — only ever assigned when an explicit deadline was resolved. Derived from reasonCode server-side; the two can never disagree.

reasonCode.description: A stable machine classification code. Intentionally an open string: consumers must treat unknown future codes as valid and fall back to the explanation. Known v1.1.0 codes: NO_QUALIFYING_REFUND, MULTIPLE_QUALIFYING_REFUNDS, CRM_STATE_INCONSISTENT, REFUND_FAILED.

policySnapshot.description: The complete immutable decision-time Policy Snapshot embedded with the action: policy identity, the rules that applied, the normalized inputs the evaluation saw, and the explainable per-rule results. Read from stored state; never re-evaluated on read.

verificationDeadlineSeconds.description: The policy's verification deadline in seconds from action acceptance (format 1.1.0), or null when this policy version sets none. When set, it is the highest-precedence deadline source of the action's frozen verification timing (deadlineSource POLICY).

policyInput.description: The normalized inputs the decision-time evaluation saw.

policyEvaluation.description: The explainable decision-time result: overall pass plus one result per rule, in policy order.
